newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Airbus ministers worried about Boeing threat.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Airbus ministers worried about Boeing threat.

text.p: German Economic Minister Guenther Rexrodt warned on Monday of potential market abuses that might arise from a planned mega-merger between aerospace and defence giants Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.
Europe's Airbus Industrie briefed ministers of the four countries in the aircraft consortium who met on Monday at the Paris air show.
Airbus partners were concerned the proposed merger between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Co could monopolise the world's aerospace business, Rexrodt told reporters.
Consortium members maintained that "the Americans are trying to monopolise the industry in terms of suppliers and customers," he said.
France's newly-appointed Commmunist transport minister Jean-Claude Gaysott said "we have decided not to accept this unfair competition."

But Britain's trade and industry minister Margaret Beckett told a news conference there was no question of anyone seeking a trade war and called for strict adherence to a 1992 aviation trade pact governing state aid to the industry.

McDonnell Douglas would give Boeing a broad position in military aircraft to go with its 60-percent market share for commercial jets. Boeing also recently agreed to deals with three big U.S. airlines to become their exclusive supplier.
Rexrodt urged the European Commission, which is reviewing the merger and the airline contracts, to look carefully to see if Boeing was gaining a dominating position.
"It must be prevented in any case where it comes to the dictation of prices for airlines and consumers," Rexrodt said in a statement.

The merger "will create a unique technology competence that gives Boeing the possibility to expand further its market position through strengthened cross-subsidies between civil and military sectors," the statement said.

"Through exclusive contracts, American airline companies will be bound to one provider, and the American market will be blocked for Airbus," it said. "These contracts document the great danger that goes out from the increasingly stronger market position of Boeing-MDD (McDonnell Douglas)."
He said all parties involved should be able to express their views before the Commission, but said Bonn would not appeal to Brussels to take action.
"The German government is not intervening in the process," he said. "The Commission has to be able to make sure the process goes ahead without interference."
